Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 1) If A and B can together do a work in 15 days and B alone can finish the job in 20 days. In how many days, A alone can finish the job?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
A and B complete a work in = 15 days
One day's work of (A + B) = 1/15
B complete the work in = 20 days;
One day's work of B = 1/20
Then, A's one day's work = 1/15 - 1/20
= (4 - 3)/60
= 1/60
Thus, A can complete the work in = 60 days.

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 2) A and B can do a work in 8 days, B and C can do the same work in 12 days. A, B and C together can finish it in 6 days. A and C together will do it in:
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
(A, B, C), In 1 day, do 1/6 part of work.
(A, B),  In 1 day do 1/8 part of  Work.

So, (A + B + C) - (A + B) = C do in 1 day (1/6 - 1/8) part of work.
= (4 - 3)/24
= 1/24

Again, (B + C), In 1 day, do 1/12 part of work.
Therefore,
(A + B + C) - (B + C) = A, in 1 day, do (1/6 - 1/12) part of work.
= (2 - 1)/12 
= 1/12

So, (A + C), In 1 day, do (1/24 + 1/12)
= (1 + 2)/24
= 1/8

So, A + C can do a job in 8 days.

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 3) X can do a piece of work in 40 days. He works at it for 8 days and then Y finishes it in 16 days. How long will they together take to complete the work?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Work done by X in 8 days = 1/40 x 8 = 1/5
Remaining work = 1 - 1/5 = 4/5

Now, 4/5 work is done by Y in 16 days.
Whole work will be done by Y in = 16 x 5/4 = 20 days.
X's 1 day's work = 1/40
Y's 1 day's work = 1/20
(X + Y)'s 1 day's work = 1/40 + 1/20 = 3/40

Hence, X and Y will together complete the work in = 40/3 = 13(1/3) days.

Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Let, A can alone the remaining job in X days.
Then,
x/18 + 10/15= 1
x = 6 days

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 5) 4 men and 6 women can complete a work in 8 days, while 3 men and 7 women can complete it in 10 Days. In how many days will 10 women complete it?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
(4M + 6W) × 8 = (3M + 7W) × 10
=> M / W = 11 : 1
Now , (4 × 11 + 6 × 1) × 8 = 10 × 1 × T
=> T = 40 days

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 6) P can complete a work in 12 days working 8 hours a day. Q can complete the same work in 8 days working 10 hours a day. If both P and Q work together, working 8 hours a day, in how many days can they complete the work?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
P's 1 day 1 hrs work = 1/96 part.
Q's 1 day 1 hr's work = 1/80 part.
P & Q together work in 1 hr per day = 1/96 + 1/80 = 11/480 part.
P & Q together completes in 8 hr per day = 11×8/480 = 11/60 part.
So, days required = 60/11 = 5(5/11)

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 7) A is 30% more efficient than B. How much time will they, working together, take to complete a job which A alone could have done in 23 days?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Ratio of times taken by A and B = 100:130 = 10:13
Suppose B takes x days to do the work.
Then,
10:13 :: 23:x
⇒ x = (23 × 13)/10
⇒ x = 299/10
A's 1 day's work = 1/23
B's 1 day's work = 10/299
(A + B)'s 1day's work = 1/23 + 10/299
= 23/299
= 1/13
∴ A and B together can complete the work in 13 days.

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 8) Robi and Kamal are working on an assignment. Robi takes 6 hours to type 32 pages on a computer, while Kamal takes 5 hours to type 40 pages. How much time will they take, working together on two different computers to type an assignment of 110 pages?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Number of pages typed by Robi in 1 hour = 32/6 = 16/3 .
Number of pages typed by Kamal in 1 hour = 40/5 = 8
Number of pages typed by both in 1 hour = (16/3 + 8) = 40/3
Therefore, Time taken by both to type 110 pages = 110/(40/3) hours
= 110 × 3/40 hours (or) 8 hours 15 minutes.

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 9) A takes twice as much time as B or thrice as much time as C to finish a piece of work. Working together, they can finish the work in 2 days. B can do the work alone in:
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Suppose A, B and C take x, x/2, x/3 days respectively to finish the work
Then,
1/x + 2/x + 3/x = 1/2
⇒ 6/x = 1/2
⇒ x = 12
So, B takes 12/2 = 6 days to finish the work.

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 10) Twenty women can do a work in sixteen days. Sixteen men can complete the same work in fifteen days. What is the ratio between the capacity of a man and a woman?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
(20 × 16) women can complete the work in 1 day
1 woman's 1day's work = 1/ 320
(16 × 15) men can complete the work in 1 day
1 man's 1day's work = 1/240
So, required ratio = 1/240 : 1/320
= 1/3 : 1/4
= 4:3

Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:

∴ Y's 1 day's work = 1/20

(X + Y)'s 1 day's work

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 12) Ayesha can complete a piece of work in 16 days. Mitu can complete the same piece of work in 8 days. If both of them work together in how many days can they complete the same piece of work?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Ayesha's 1 day's work = 1/16
Mitu's 1 day's work = 1/8
(Ayesha + Mithu)'s 1 day's work
= 1/16 + 1/8
= 3/16

∴ Both together can complete the work in = 16/3
= 5(1/3) days

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 13) A can do a piece of work in 10 days, B in 15 days. They work together for 5 days, the rest of the work is finished by C in two more days. If they get Rs. 3000 as wages for the whole work, what are the daily wages of A, B and C respectively:
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
A's 5 days work = 50%
B's 5 days work = 33.33%
C's 2 days work = 16.66% [100 - (50 + 33.33)]

Ratio of contribution of work of A, B and C = 50: 33(1/3) : 16(2/3)
= 3 : 2 : 1

A's total share = Tk. 1500
B's total share = Tk. 1000
C's total share = Tk. 500

A's one day's earning = Tk.300
B's one day's earning = Tk.200
C's one day's earning = Tk.250

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 14) A, B, C together can do a piece of work in 10 days. All the three started working at it together and after 4 days, A left. Then, B and C together completed the work in 10 more days. In how many days A can complete the work alone?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
(A + B + C) do 1 work in 10 days.

So (A + B + C)'s 1 day work = 1/10
And as they work together for 4 days,
so, work done by them in 4 days = 4/10 = 2/5
Remaining work = 1 - (2/5) = 3/5
(B + C) takes 10 more days to complete 3/5 work.
So ( B+C)'s 1 day work = 3/50
Now A's 1 day work = (A + B + C)'s 1 day work - (B + C)'s 1 day work
= 1/10 - 3/50
= 1/25
A does 1/25 work in in 1 day
Therefore 1 work in 25 days.

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 15) A works twice as fast as B. If B can complete a work in 18 days independently, the number of days in which A and B can together finish the work is:
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Ratio of rates of working of A and B = 2:1.
So, ratio of times taken = 1:2
Therefore, A's 1 day's work = 1/9
B's 1 day's work = 1/18
(A + B)'s 1 day's work = 1/9 + 1/18 = 1/6
So, A and B together can finish the work in 6 days.

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 16) A is thrice efficient as B and C is twice as efficient as B. What is the ratio of number of days taken by A,B and C, when they work individually?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
A : B : C
Ratio of efficiency - 3 : 1 : 2
Ratio of No. of days - 1/3 : 1/1 : 1/2
or 2 : 6 : 3

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 17) 4 men can repair a road in 7 hours. How many men are required to repair the road in 2 hours?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
4 men can repair a road in 7 hours
1 men can repair a road in 7 × 4hours = 28 hours
28 hours is required by 1 men
2 hours is required by 28/2 men = 14 men

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 18) A, B and C can complete a piece of work in 24, 6 and 12 days respectively. Working together, they will complete the same work in:
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
(A + B + C)'s 1 day's work = (1/24 + 1/6 + 1/12) = 7/24
so, A, B and C together will complete the work in 24/7 days.

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 19) When A, B and C are deployed for a task , A and B together do 70% of the work and B and C together do 50% of the work. Who is most efficient?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
A + B = 70%
B + C = 50%
[∵ (A + B) + (B + C) − (A + B + C) = B]
=> B = 20% ; A = 50% and C = 30%
Hence A is most efficient.

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 20) A can do a piece of work in 30 days. He works at it for 6 days and then B finishes it in 18 days. In what time can A and B together it?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Let 'B' alone can do the work in 'x' days
6/30 + 18/x = 1
=> x = 22.5
1/30 + 1/22.5 = 7/90
=> 90/7 = 12 (6/7) days

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 21) If a quarter kg of carrots costs 60 poysa, how many poysa will 200 gms cost?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Quarter of Kg means 250 gm
Less weight, less price (Direct Proportion)
So, 250 : 200 :: 60 : x
=> x = 48
So 200 gm will cost 48 poysa.

Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
1 2 3 4 5 6 (Shahadat) 7 (Nitu) 8 (Altaf) 9 10 11 12 13 14

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 23) If a person has Tk. 2000 and he wants to distribute this to his five children in the manner that each son has Tk. 30 more than the younger one, what will be the share of the youngest child?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Assume first child (the youngest) get = Tk. x
According to the question ;
each son having Tk. 30 more than the younger one

Second child will get = Tk. x + 30
Third child will get = Tk. x + 30 + 30 = x + 60
Fourth child will get = Tk. x + 30 + 30 + 30 = x + 90
Fifth child will get = Tk. x + 30 + 30 + 30 + 30 = x + 120

Total amount they got = Tk. 2000

x + (x+30) + (x+60) + (x+90) + (x+120) = 2000
5x + 300 = 2000
5x = 1700
x = Tk. 340
So the youngest child will get Tk. 340.

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 24) A contractor undertakes to do a piece of work in 40 days. He engages 100 men at the beginning and 100 more after 35 days and completes the work in stipulated time. If he had not engaged the additional men, how many days behind schedule would it be finished?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
[(100 × 35) + (200 × 5)]men can finish the work in 1 day.
Therefore, 4500 men can finish the work in 1 day. 100 men can finish it in = 4500/100 = 45 days.
This is 5 days behind Schedule

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 25) A certain number of men can finish a piece of work in 100 days. If there were 10 men less, it would take 10 days more for the work to be finished. How many men were there originally?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Originally let there be x men.

Less men, More days (Indirect Proportion)

Therefore, (x - 10) : x :: 100 :110

=> (x - 10) × 110 = x × 100
=> x = 110

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 26) 3 pumps working 8 hours a day, can empty a tank in 2 days. How many hours a day must 4 pumps work to empty the tank in 1 day?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Let the required number of working hours per day be x.
More pumps , Less working hours per day (Indirect Proportion)
Less days, More working hours per day (Indirect Proportion)
Pumps 4 : 3 and Days 1 : 2 } :: 8:x
=> (4 × 1 × x) = (3 × 2 × 8)
=> x = 12

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 27) If the Price of 6 toys is Tk. 264.37. What will be the approximate price of 5 toys?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Let the required Price be Tk. X .
Then, Lest toys , Less cost (Direct Proportion)
Therefore 6 : 5 :: 264.37 : x
=> 6 × x = 5 × 264.37
=> x = 220.308
Therefore, Approximate price of 5 toys = Tk. 220

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 28) A fort had provision of food for 150 men for 45 days. After 10 days, 25 men left the fort. The number of days for which the remaining food will last, is:
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
After 10 days : 150 men had food for 35 days.
Suppose 125 men had food for x days.
Now, Less men, More days (Indirect Proportion)
∴ 125 : 150 :: 35 : x
⇒ 125 × x = 150 × 35
⇒ x = (150 × 35)/125
= 42

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 29) If 7 spiders make 7 webs in 7 days, then 1 spider will make 1 web in how many days?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Let the required number of days be x.
Less spiders, More days (Indirect Proportion)
Less webs, Less days (Direct Proportion)
Spiders 1:7 and Webs 7:1 } :: 7:x
=> 1 × 7 × x = 7 × 1 × 7
=> x = 7

Time & Work, Chain Rule.question: 30) Running at the same constant rate, 6 identical machines can produce a total of 270 bottles per minute. At this rate, how many bottles could 10 such machines produce in 4 minutes?
Time & Work, Chain Rule.exp:
Let the required number of bottles be x.
More machines, More bottles (Direct Proportion)
More minutes, More bottles (Direct Proportion)
Machines 6:10 and time(in min) 1:4 } :: 270:x
=> 6 × 1 × x = 10 × 4 × 270
=> x = 1800
